evidence.requirements: Every brief item is met. The three tastings are defined exactly in shared/catalog.ts:13-38. The start page shows title, date/time, 'EUR n per guest' and '<n> seats left' (CataloguePage.tsx:75-94, start.jpg), and each card has a 'Book <title>' link (CataloguePage.tsx:98-103). The form has Name/Email/Guests fields limited to 1-8 and a 'Book' button (BookingPage.tsx:109-135, form.jpg). Seat limits are enforced on the server (store.ts:77-79) and errors appear next to their field (Field.tsx:32-36, form.jpg). The confirmation shows 'Booking confirmed', the tasting, guests, total and reference (ConfirmationPage.tsx:57-79, confirmation.jpg). /staff has a 'Password' field and 'Sign in' button, reads STAFF_PASSWORD from the environment (config.ts:19), groups bookings by tasting with name, email, guests and reference, and has a 'Cancel' button that frees seats (StaffPage.tsx:197-235, store.ts:98-100, staff.jpg). The app uses React, Express 5, react-router, react-hook-form, zod and Tailwind, keeps bookings in memory, serves on PORT with 3000 as the default (config.ts:12), and is in English. Only nit: opening the booking URL of a sold-out tasting directly still shows the form, and it is rejected only on submit (app.ts:102-104).
evidence.correctness: Checking and inserting a booking happen in one synchronous step (store.ts:74-91), so concurrent requests cannot oversell. A test fires 50 simultaneous bookings at 3 free seats (store.test.ts:129-142). Too many guests returns a 409 with the seats left attached to the Guests field (app.ts:105-108), and a full tasting returns a form-level 409. Cancelling deletes the booking, so seatsLeft is recomputed. A second cancel returns 404 and the UI refreshes (StaffPage.tsx:67-69). Cancelled references are never reused (store.ts:109-114). Validation trims input and checks bounds: 100-character name, 254-character email, guests a whole number from 1 to 8, with text coerced to a number (validation.ts:8-28). Malformed JSON gets a JSON 400 (app.ts:194-196). Dates are formatted without time-zone shifts (format.ts:30-34). I found no logic defects.
evidence.security: The password check hashes both sides with SHA-256 and compares with timingSafeEqual (staff.ts:21-27). Session tokens are 32 random bytes kept in memory, in an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie (app.ts:139-143). Sign-out invalidates the token server-side (staff.ts:39-41). Failed sign-ins are rate-limited (app.ts:51-60), the JSON body is capped at 10kb, x-powered-by is disabled, and an empty STAFF_PASSWORD disables sign-in. React escapes all output and there are no secrets in the code. Weaknesses: the cookie has no Secure flag and sessions never expire server-side. The rate limiter keys on req.ip with no 'trust proxy' setting, so behind the reverse proxy the README recommends, ten wrong guesses from anyone lock out all staff for 15 minutes. There are no security headers such as CSP.
evidence.code_quality: The code splits cleanly into shared/ (catalog, zod schemas used by both client and server, formatting), server/ (createApp factory, BookingStore, StaffSessions, config) and client/ (pages, one Field component, a small api wrapper). Load states are discriminated unions (BookingPage.tsx:11-15), store results are typed (store.ts:20-24), naming is clear and comments are sparse and purposeful. Errors are handled consistently, with a JSON error middleware (app.ts:189-200). Small redundancies: findTasting exists both in shared/catalog.ts:40 and in BookingStore, and the 'unknown-tasting' branch in app.ts:99 cannot be reached after the check at app.ts:85.
evidence.tests: The tests cover every layer. Store tests cover boundaries, the full and partly full cases, cancellation, reference uniqueness and concurrency (store.test.ts). Supertest API tests cover validation messages, the 409 cases, 404s, malformed JSON and the confirmation hiding name and email (guest-api.test.ts). Staff tests cover the cookie flags, wrong, empty and unconfigured passwords, forged cookies, sign-out and the rate limit (staff.test.ts). Component tests check accessible descriptions for field errors and the server error paths (BookingPage.test.tsx, StaffPage.test.tsx). A Playwright suite runs the full guest-to-staff-cancel flow, the seat limit, the fully booked state, a wrong password, and phone and desktop overflow checks (e2e/tastings.spec.ts). The tests map directly to the brief's requirements.
evidence.ux_design: start.jpg, form.jpg, confirmation.jpg and staff.jpg show a coherent winery look: wine-red header, cream paper background, serif headings and clear cards. Availability is green, sold out has a grey 'Fully booked' badge, the confirmation sits in a green panel, and the field error is red and appears directly under Email (form.jpg). The staff table is easy to scan and shows 'x of y seats booked' per tasting, and it stacks into blocks on phones (StaffPage.tsx:195-226). Downsides: the design is plain, with no imagery or brand atmosphere. The booking form does not show how many seats are left. Staff 'Cancel' takes effect on one click with no confirmation or undo (StaffPage.tsx:228-233), which is risky for a real booking list.
evidence.accessibility: Labels are tied to inputs with htmlFor/id, and errors are linked through aria-describedby with aria-invalid set (Field.tsx:18-36). react-hook-form focuses the first invalid field. Form-level errors use role=alert. Pages use landmarks (header, main, footer), sections and articles labelled by headings, dl/dt/dd for details, real table headers on desktop with screen-reader-only headers on phones, html lang='en', and visible focus rings. Gaps: field errors are not live regions, and server-set errors do not move focus. Every 'Cancel' button has the same accessible name, with no booking context. The grey sold-out text (#8a7f76 on a tinted cream, text-sm) is about 3.8:1, below WCAG AA for small text (index.css:14, CataloguePage.tsx:69).
evidence.simplicity: Dependencies fit the problem and the brief's request for established libraries: express, cookie-parser, express-rate-limit, react, react-router, react-hook-form with zod, and Tailwind. There is no database and no state library. Total code is moderate, roughly 1,000 lines without tests. Some extras go beyond the brief but stay small: the rate limiter, the reference-reuse set (store.ts:48-49), a 'not configured' state, and the dev setup with concurrently.
evidence.maintainability: The README covers install, build, start, the environment variable table, dev, test and e2e commands, how to install Playwright, and operating caveats: memory-only storage, single process, the need for HTTPS (README.md:14-47). A package-lock.json is present, typecheck is a script, and there are many regression tests. Missing: no CI pipeline config, no changelog or release process beyond version 1.0.0, and no ADRs. The README points to openspec/changes/add-tasting-bookings, but the repo only has openspec/specs/.gitkeep (README.md:56). Node is unpinned (engines '>=22', no .nvmrc), and dependencies use caret ranges. There is no staff manual beyond the README's two lines.

unmet_requirements: Partly met: opening the booking URL of a sold-out tasting directly still shows the form; the fully booked state only appears after submitting (BookingPage.tsx has no seatsLeft === 0 branch).
strengths: Seat limits are correct and atomic: checking and inserting happen in one synchronous step, cancelled references are never reused, and server-side zod validation is shared with the client form so errors appear next to the right field.
Thorough tests at every layer (store, supertest API, React Testing Library, Playwright e2e on phone and desktop) map directly to the brief, including concurrency, boundaries, cancellation and auth.
Solid staff security for the scope: constant-time password comparison, random in-memory session tokens in HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookies, server-side sign-out and a rate limit on failed sign-ins.
issues: Staff 'Cancel' deletes a booking on a single click with no confirmation or undo, and every Cancel button has the same accessible name (StaffPage.tsx:228-233).

Session and proxy hardening is incomplete: the cookie has no Secure flag, sessions never expire server-side, and the rate limiter keys on req.ip without 'trust proxy', so behind a reverse proxy anyone can lock all staff out (app.ts:51-60, 139-143).
Maintenance gaps: no CI pipeline, no changelog or versioning process, no ADRs, the README references an openspec change that is not in the repo, and the Node version is not pinned beyond '>=22'.
review.verdict: This is a well-built, correct and well-tested booking app that meets every requirement in the brief, with a coherent winery look that works on phones. Before handing it to the winery I would add a confirmation step for staff cancellations, a Secure cookie with session expiry and trust-proxy handling, and a CI pipeline.
